question.worked_solution:
We must factor the quadratic expression

$$
2{x}^{2}+7x+6.
$$

First, we find two numbers that 

- multiply to the product of the quadratic coefficient and the constant ($2\times 6=12$), and

- add to the linear coefficient ($7$).

Since all coefficients are positive, we only need to consider the positive factor pairs of $12.$

The positive factor pairs of $12$ are

$$
(1,12),\,(2,6),\,(3,4).
$$

Notice the numbers in the factor pair $(3,4)$ add to $7:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}3+4 & =7\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we write the linear term as $3x+4x,$ and factor the result by grouping:

$$
\begin{aligned}2{x}^{2}+7x+6 & = \\ 2{x}^{2}+3x+4x+6 & = \\ (2{x}^{2}+3x)+(4x+6) & = \\ x(2x+3)+2(2x+3) & = \\ (x+2)(2x+3) & \end{aligned}
$$
